My research lies at the intersections of theoretical computer science, data science, and machine learning. In particular, I am currently interested in numerical linear algebra, streaming algorithms, and differential privacy. **I'm looking for PhD students and postdocs interested in broadly working in sublinear algorithms, differential privacy, or the theoretical foundations of machine learning, for the Fall 2026 cycle. **For Texas A&M University undergraduate students: If you are interested in research and have a solid background in computer science and/or mathematics, feel free to reach out anytime to explore opportunities.**.

results.title: IMI AI/ML Fellowships, 2026: High risk research
results.content: This document describes the research topics we are opening for fellowships. Each topic suggests several projects indicative of the scope and complexity we expect you to undertake. 10 places are open for the 2026 term, with a duration of 6 or 12 months at the applicant's option. The intent of these fellowships is to give awardees uninterrupted time to focus on harder open problems, with adequate compute, talented peers, and weekly 1:1 mentorship from senior researchers but without chasing specific metrics. You will be expected to spend about 80% of your time on your own research, and up to 20% of your time either assisting other fellows or participating in wider research programs at IMI. At the end of your fellowship, if the threshold for refereed publication is unmet we will expect a final report, which may be published as a blog post.
